name: Luis Figo
years: b. 4 Nov 1972; pro career 1989-2009; Ballon d'Or 2000

recent_news.headline: FIFA confirms three presidential candidates for 2027; Figo is not one of them
facts: On 19 Nov 2026 FIFA confirmed three candidacies for the 18 March 2027 election in Rabat: Gianni Infantino, Philippe Diallo (French FA president) and Kohzo Tashima (ex-Japan FA president).
Luis Figo, who had been named as a possible UEFA-backed challenger, did not enter; the nomination deadline passed on 18 Nov.
Diallo was endorsed by the UEFA Executive Committee and European FIFA Council members (Wikipedia); O Jogo's 'unanimous' wording could not be checked (HTTP 403).
recent_news.note: Punchline material: the 'candidate' who never became one.

recent_news.headline: UEFA reportedly tries to persuade Figo to challenge Infantino for the FIFA presidency
facts: On 16 Nov 2026 French outlet Foot Mercato reported that several UEFA officials wanted Figo to run, two days before the 18 Nov nomination deadline.
Figo came up after Arsene Wenger declined and Hungarian FA chief Sandor Csanyi was considered (A Bola says Csanyi also declined); the idea was not unanimous inside UEFA.
A candidate needs backing from at least five FIFA member associations; the vote is 18 March 2027 in Rabat, Morocco. Figo himself had not announced anything.

recent_news.headline: Sky Sports (as relayed by a Brazilian outlet): Figo among names UEFA weighs against Infantino
facts: A report credited to Sky Sports on 15 Oct 2026 listed Figo, Arsene Wenger and Michelle Kang (Eagle Football Group) among possible challengers to Infantino.
The relayed report says Figo had not announced a run and that rivals could wait until the 18 Nov deadline.
recent_news.note: Relay page opened and matches; original Sky Sports page not opened.

recent_news.headline: Figo trades barbs on X with Catalan politician Gabriel Rufian; 'Figo the mercenary' resurfaces
facts: At an ERC rally in Tarragona on Friday 13 Nov Rufian joked that a hypothetical PP-Vox government could make Figo sports minister.
Figo replied on X on Sunday 15 Nov that Rufian had gone from uniting the left to ending up with Podemos and wished him luck for the 29th; Goal says Figo later deleted a post.
Rufian answered 'Not all of us sell ourselves' and reposted the old 'Figo pesetero' banknote image tied to Figo's 2000 move from Barcelona to Real Madrid.
Figo then added 'Ya no vendes ni humo!!!' (OKDiario, 16 Nov).
The exchange came less than two weeks before Spain's 29 Nov 2026 general election.
recent_news.note: Partisan politics during a live election campaign: use ONLY the 'mercenary' transfer history for jokes, never take a side on the politics.

recent_news.headline: Figo tells El Pais (via Record) he is launching his own clothing brand as an 'industrial project, not a hobby'
facts: Figo says the clothing brand under his own name, built with a business partner, is 'an industrial project, not a hobby'.
He told El Pais that his name can help early promotion but 'the name guarantees you nothing' and the product must stand on quality.
On critics he said: if God does not please everyone, imagine Luis Figo; he also called free time and independence 'the luxury' of today.
recent_news.note: Record (19 Nov) reports that Figo told El Pais; the El Pais original was not opened. The sources give no launch year and no brand name; the earlier '2024' and 'LF Luis Figo' were not supported.

recent_news.headline: Figo on Real Madrid: Vinicius will return to form, Diomande quick and a goal threat, credit to Mourinho
facts: Figo said Vinicius Jr 'will return to his level, to his status'; he called Yan Diomande quick and a goal threat whose defensive work matters, and said Arda Guler's involvement shows his quality.
He said credit for Real Madrid's good run belongs to Jose Mourinho's decisions and the players, citing better solidity.
Madrid Universal (via Yahoo) describes him as a Betfair ambassador.

recent_news.headline: Figo turns 54: 'It is just a number'
facts: Figo turned 54 on Wednesday 4 Nov 2026 and posted on Instagram that '54 is just a number'.
recent_news.note: Age joke is mild; do not reference the family in the post.

recent_news.headline: Figo predicts a 2-2 Clasico and says he could have started for either team
facts: Before the 25 Oct 2026 Clasico Figo predicted 2-2 at Camp Nou with goals from Raphinha, Lamine Yamal, Bellingham and Mbappe.
He said that at his level of 26 years ago he could have been a starter for either team, and that if he coached either side he would pick himself: 'si no lo digo yo, nadie lo dirá'.
He said Mourinho could have been a good Barcelona coach and that, had he overlapped with Lamine Yamal, he might have had to move to the left.
recent_news.note: Libertad Digital identifies him as a Betfair ambassador but does not say the remarks come from a Betfair interview.

recent_news.headline: The Clasico ends Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid, not the 2-2 Figo predicted
facts: Real Madrid won 2-1 at Camp Nou on 25 Oct 2026: Mbappe scored in the first half and in the 87th minute; Raphinha equalised in between.
Of Figo's four predicted scorers, only Mbappe and Raphinha scored; Yamal and Bellingham did not score.
recent_news.note: Joke is on his prediction, not on any person's misfortune.

recent_news.headline: Figo seen at the Open de Espana golf at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid
facts: Getty photo caption (via Caras) shows Figo at the Club de Campo Villa de Madrid for day two of the Open de Espana on 9 October; the caption gives no year, so 2026 is inferred.

recent_news.headline: Figo on Radio MARCA: Real Madrid will fight to the end; Mbappe 'one of the best in the world' at scoring
facts: Figo said Real Madrid would fight until the very end and that Barcelona had started strong, but the season is long.
Asked about Mourinho's comments on referees after the Madrid derby, he declined to judge and said he had not watched because he was in Zurich.
On the Ballon d'Or he said he does not vote, so he would not comment.

recent_news.headline: Figo praises Real Madrid's summer signings but says transfer fees are 'crazy' and hard to justify
facts: Figo praised Real Madrid's summer business (six signings in key positions) as 'necessary' after two seasons without a major trophy.
On Diomande's reported EUR 140m fee he said the price reflects the market, and that a EUR 150m deal is hard to recoup through merchandise sales.

recent_news.headline: [Outside 90-day window, explains current story] Figo says Infantino 'should go. Now.'
facts: On 5 Aug 2026 Euronews reported that Figo posted on X that Infantino 'debased the office that he promised to elevate' and 'lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest'.
A Bola and a Sky relay describe a Daily Mail op-ed/open letter by Figo in August calling for Infantino to step down.
It came after Infantino scrapped a plan for private minority stakes in a new FIFA commercial unit.
recent_news.note: Euronews opened. '10,000 words / three words' not found and removed. Euronews does not call Figo a UEFA adviser. These are Figo's own accusations: always attribute ('Figo said').

quick_context: Figo won the 2000 Ballon d'Or (he scored 14 goals in 51 games for Barcelona in 1999-2000) and the 2001 FIFA World Player of the Year after a record EUR 62m move to Real Madrid. He won four La Liga titles, one Champions League and four Serie A titles, and played 127 times for Portugal, reaching the Euro 2000 semi-finals and the Euro 2004 final. He retired at Inter in 2009.

claims.claim: On 19 Nov 2026 FIFA confirmed three candidacies for the 18 March 2027 election in Rabat: Gianni Infantino, Philippe Diallo (French FA president) and Kohzo Tashima (ex-Japan FA president).

The relayed report says Figo had not officially announced a run and that rivals could wait until the 18 Nov deadline; it also notes Figo wrote a Daily Mail op-ed in August calling for Infantino to step down.
